analysis:
The PR only changes docs/provider/two-mac-cluster.md (head lines 49-75): it adds a documentation section, "The cluster waitlist", about `darkbloom waitlist cluster`. No code, protocol, key handling, attestation, or authorization logic changes in this diff. Head lines 60-61 say the command sends nothing about the user's Macs, only the account. Lines 67-75 say a new pair serving through Darkbloom needs waitlist approval, that `darkbloom cluster local` needs none, and that already-paired Macs are never asked and keep working. The base excerpt (lines 1313-1667) is unchanged context.

Security relevance: the waitlist gate is an account-level admission and approval control, not a serving-authorization control. The documented approval is not stated to replace the App Attest or coordinator serving-authorization checks (A-016, TB-011, T-052, T-053), and nothing in this doc says it does. The grandfathering of already-paired Macs (lines 73-74) is a policy statement. Whether the CLI and backend enforce it correctly cannot be verified from the supplied evidence. The CLI waitlist implementation, the cli-reference anchor and the coordinator endpoint are not supplied. The server-side enforcement is platform-owned and out of scope for this repo's threat model.

T-041, the one definition supplied in full, concerns the prefix cache and is not touched by this doc change. Prior analyses were not relied on. I found no regression or new attack surface. The only open question for later review is whether the actual CLI waitlist code matches these claims, in particular that it sends no machine data and cannot be used to bypass serving authorization.
